secondary.topic: Status of the §7c critic pass for this spine
secondary.a: Treats the scenario's silence as a clean review and applies the `none` row — 'The scenario reports no findings, so the disposition is none: Write nothing. No veto_add call, no class change.'
secondary.b: Treats the pass as not yet discharged — 'The critic veto (§7c) is still owed as an independent third judgment and can only push flesh → bone, never the reverse.'
secondary.governing_quote: If no finding on a spine passes Gate A — the review was clean, or its only remarks were cosmetic — the disposition is `none`
secondary.source: plan-release/references/critic-veto.md §3 (with the parallel row in plan-release/SKILL.md §7c)
secondary.explanation: The prose defines `none` only over a review that actually returned findings, and separately defines the `absent`-critic path (§7c step 1, 'warn once and continue with the §7a/§7b judgments only'); it gives no vocabulary for 'the pass has not been run yet', which is the state this scenario presents. That gap is what let two planners read identical evidence as a discharged disposition (A) versus an outstanding obligation (B). Low-stakes: both conclude the critic cannot change the class here, since bone-touch-judge §1 forbids a clean critic clearing a touch hit and a veto only pushes flesh → bone.

notes: All five axes agree, in most cases on the same governing sentences and the same excluded alternatives (kill switch, CLI surface, system-shape pressure bar), so this run produces no finding against the shipped prose on the scored axes. The only asymmetries are one narrative difference over whether the §7c critic pass is already discharged, plus unilateral additions neither planner contradicts — B's paper-env-vs-`auto:`-line consequence for plan-spine §8a and its 'posture owes no controls' note, and A's observation that the sketch's 'next: v1' hypothesis is already stale.
